reasoning:
Recent general-election polling in Michigan’s 2026 Senate race shows a very tight contest between Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers, with most high-quality polls and aggregates indicating roughly a 1–3 point Republican edge, while one independent aggregate based only on El-Sayed–Rogers matchups shows the race as essentially a tie or microscopic Democratic advantage.[1][10][12] Given these mixed but narrow results, the current effective margin in Michigan’s 2026 Senate race is best characterized as approximately R+1 to R+2, consistent with major forecasters still rating the race as a toss-up but with a slight Republican polling edge.[2][10][12]

Michigan’s Cook Partisan Voting Index statewide is D+1, meaning in recent presidential elections the state has voted about one point more Democratic than the national average.[12]

sources.name: PollsMax
sources.details: PollsMax’s 2026 Michigan Senate polling average for Abdul El-Sayed vs. Mike Rogers shows 44.3% for El-Sayed and 43.9% for Rogers, an average margin of D+0.4 in a very close race based on 13 polls, last updated July 6, 2026.
sources.date_range: through July 6, 2026 (aggregate of polls, latest poll June 30, 2026)

sources.name: EPIC-MRA (reported by The New York Times)
sources.details: An EPIC-MRA poll sponsored by MIRS, reported by The New York Times, finds Mike Rogers leading Abdul El-Sayed 46% to 43% in the Michigan Senate general-election matchup, a margin of R+3.

sources.name: EPIC-MRA (reported by The New York Times)
sources.details: The same EPIC-MRA/MIRS polling series also tested Haley Stevens vs. Mike Rogers and found Stevens leading Rogers 44% to 42%, a margin of D+2, illustrating that Rogers runs slightly stronger against El-Sayed than against Stevens.

sources.name: Sabato’s Crystal Ball (University of Virginia Center for Politics)
sources.details: Sabato’s Crystal Ball notes that in RacetotheWH polling averages before the Democratic primary, Haley Stevens led Mike Rogers about 44.5% to 43.5% (D+1), while Abdul El-Sayed trailed Rogers 45% to 43% (R+2), reinforcing a slight GOP edge against El-Sayed and a near-toss-up overall.

sources.name: Cook Political Report (via The Hill)
sources.details: The Hill reports that the Cook Political Report rates the open Michigan Senate race as a 'toss up,' indicating no clear structural advantage for either party despite Republicans targeting the seat for a flip.
